paragraph: On 2 July 2026 INE [launched the Census 2024 Portal and the INE Angola app in Uíge](<https://angop.ao/noticias/politica/ine-lanca-portal-do-censo-2024-e-aplicacao-movel/>). Its head said INE's own technical staff built them. In the last twelve months, [INFOSI opened the government's Data Center and Cloud in April 2026](<https://pti.ao/mario-oliveira-inauguracao-do-data-center-e-cloud-do-governo-constitui-um-passo-gigante-rumo-a-soberania-digital/>). The tax authority AGT is building its own AI risk-analysis system, [tested since 2024](<https://correiokianda.info/inteligencia-artificial-coloca-incumpridores-sob-analise-reforcada-da-agt/>) and not stated to be live. No source found since October 2023 names three systems run wholly by government staff. Mature would need three or more systems run, maintained and changed by government staff, with no contractor, by a source from the past three years.

No stage is set. [SETIC, Burundi's government ICT secretariat, lists software development and hosting for public institutions among its services](<https://setic.gov.bi/?pages%2F10253095=>). It also lists [operating and maintaining the network and systems infrastructure of public institutions](<https://setic.gov.bi/?pages%2F10253095=>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says a government body's own technical staff run, maintain or support one of its named systems. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later saying government's own staff run, maintain or built one of its systems.

On 1 November 2026 the Justice Ministry's own information systems directorate [led the instant criminal-record service that went live on service-public.bj](<https://www.linfodrome.com/international/127167-benin-wadagni-concretise-sa-promesse-le-casier-judiciaire-instantane-a-1-900-fcfa>). No contractor is named. In the last twelve months, ASIN [developed the signature, encryption and secure messaging tools issued to 300 police officers](<https://www.dgpr.bj/techniques-de-protection-des-informations-sensibles-de-letat-lagence-des-systemes-dinformation-et-du-numerique-asin-et-direction-des-systemes-dinformation-et-de/>) in mid-2026. In August 2026 ASIN [gave the private integrator MAPCOM a two-year contract to maintain the state data centre](<https://lamarina.bj/2026/08/24/souverainete-tech-comment-la-sbin-sest-fait-evincer-dun-contrat-cle-de-lasin/>). [Cybernetica says it still helps Benin maintain the citizen portal and the data exchange platform](<https://cyber.ee/resources/case-studies/benin/>). Mature would need three or more systems run, maintained and changed by government staff, with no contractor, by a source from the past three years.

On 2 April 2024 the digital ministry [launched the ATI platform, developed in-house by its own directorates](<https://gouvernement.gov.bf/actualites/dematerialisation-des-procedures-de-ladministration-la-plateforme-ati-lancee-officiellement/>). The state ICT agency ANPTIC lists [the government systems it has developed](<https://anptic.gov.bf/nos-realisations/>), among them Toumnana (SIGED) and SIGEPE. That page is undated. In the last twelve months, on 3 April 2026, the Treasury's director general said [Lanaya and e-BDT were developed by the Treasury's own administration](<https://www.sidwaya.info/tresor-public-lanaya-et-e-bdt-pour-simplifier-les-demarches-administratives/>). On 3 September 2026 ANPTIC [helped design the ANAGRASC claims-registration platform](<https://burkina24.com/2026/09/03/burkina-faso-lancement-dune-plateforme-pour-le-recensement-du-passif-de-trois-societes-immobilieres/>), when it was launched.

The Botswana Examinations Council's 2024/25 annual report says [DataSmart was built in-house, developed and deployed that year](<https://www.bec.co.bw/images/2025/annual-report/bec-annual-report-2025-final-09-12-25_.pdf>). It captures marks for the PSLE, JCE and BGCSE at all three levels. The communications minister said government services are housed at [the Department of Shared Digital Services](<https://www.mmegi.bw/business/govt-moves-to-in-house-local-data/news>), in a statement published in November 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The Council's other systems, Malepa, e-marking and e-authoring, are not said to be built in-house. Mature would need three or more systems run, maintained and changed by government staff, with no contractor, by a source from the past three years.

In September 2026 Expertise France advertised for [local IT experts to run the tax directorate's servers and administer SIGICA](<https://expertise-france.gestmax.fr/i5pour100/16150/1/safe-rca-expert-e-local-e-en-informatique-h-f>), the tax system. The posts belong to SAFE, an EU-funded project for the finance ministry. SIGICA's publisher and an outside contractor deliver its modules and the SIM_ba budget system. That posting is the one fact found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says government staff run or maintain any of its systems. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later saying government's own staff run, maintain or built one of its systems.

On 25 July 2024 GUCE CI launched [GUCE Mobile, a five-module app built and run entirely by its own teams](<https://www.gucecotedivoire.ci/innovation-et-dematerialisation-dans-lecosysteme-du-commerce-exterieur-guce-ci-lance-sa-nouvelle-application-guce-mobile-tant-attendue-par-les-operateurs-economiques-les-acteurs-majeurs-e/>). In the last twelve months, in July 2026, Ivoirexpress said [the state company SNDI built SIGFIP for public finance, SIGOMAP, and the CEPICI one-stop shop for business formalities](<https://ivoirexpress.ci/2026/07/28/digitalisation-des-services-publics-en-cote-divoire-les-applications-metiers-developpees-par-la-sndi/>). It also built the building-permit one-stop system. No contractor is named for any of them. In September 2026 an SNDI representative said [it has run its own satellite network since 2006](<https://afriksoir.net/aspex-2026-le-satellite-au-coeur-des-enjeux-de-connectivite-et-de-resilience-numerique-en-cote-divoire/>).

In May 2026 a webinar record said [the health ministry's IT unit and the universal health coverage cell govern and administer the CSU openIMIS platform](<https://openimis.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OP/pages/5154603013/Webinaire+Souverainet+Appropriation+des+syst+mes+de+sant+num+riques>). The ministry handles day-to-day operations, and advanced work still needs outside support. That record is the one fact found in the last twelve months. The ministry runs openIMIS but is not said to have built it. No source found from 2023 or later says a government body builds or runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

[In August 2024 the French Treasury's sheet on Congo's digital sector said the tax system E-TAX was built in-house](<https://www.tresor.economie.gouv.fr/Pays/CG/le-secteur-du-numerique>), by the finance ministry's information systems directorate. The sheet gives no launch date. [In December 2024 Les Dépêches de Brazzaville said the digital economy agency Aden ensures the technical management of the government portal gouvernement.cg](<https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/numerique-laden-examine-ses-documents-cadres-161959>). On 22 July 2025 the finance ministry [installed 18 heads and assistants in that directorate](<https://www.finances.gouv.cg/fr/articles/direction-des-syst%C3%A8mes-d%E2%80%99information-dsi-du-minist%C3%A8re-des-finances>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a system built by government staff, not a contractor, to go live within the last three years.

In May 2026 the head of information systems at the health insurer AMG said [its openIMIS system still depends heavily on external developers](<https://openimis.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OP/pages/5154603013/Webinaire+Souverainet+Appropriation+des+syst+mes+de+sant+num+riques>). Only two local developers had been trained, and the local firm ETECH was not operating. That statement is the one fact found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says government staff run or maintain any of its systems. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later saying government's own staff run, maintain or built one of its systems.

In March 2026 the state company NOSi [formally handed over the Justice Information System](<https://www.governo.cv/nosi-faz-entrega-formal-do-sistema-de-informacao-da-justica-ao-ministerio-da-justica/>), whose SIPP criminal-case part its team developed. It is in use in every comarca. In the last twelve months, [NOSi ran the site that published the May 2026 legislative election results](<https://www.anacao.cv/noticia/2026/05/18/legislativas-2026-presidente-do-nosi-pede-desculpas-por-alegado-ciber-ataque-durante-a-divulgacao-dos-resultados-das-eleicoes/>). NOSi [runs the election-results system and portal eleicoes.cv with its own staff](<https://www.anacao.cv/noticia/2026/05/27/legislativas-2026-nosi-diz-que-relatorio-preliminar-aponta-para-causas-de-ordem-tecnica/>). In October 2024 [the finance ministry's technology team worked to restore the SIGOF finance system](<https://expressodasilhas.cv/pais/2024/10/11/instabilidade-no-sigof-pode-causar-atrasos-nos-pagamentos-do-estado/93685>).

On 14 January 2025 [the Council of Ministers approved a 2025 budget of 556.7 million FDJ for ANSIE](<https://www.presidence.dj/conseil-des-ministres/2025-01-14>), the state information systems agency. It pays for work for administrations, among them the E-JO and E-BALO platforms, archive digitisation, a human-resources system and the social registry. ANSIE is itself building a third version of E-JO. [Estonia's eGA helped ANSIE set up a data exchange layer in 2022 and 2023](<https://ega.ee/project/djibouti-digital-interoperability-platform/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a system built by government staff went live since October 2023. Operating would need a system built by government staff, not a contractor, to go live within the last three years.

On 11 January 2026 the state property directorate [extended Amlak to all its cadastre and land offices](<https://algeriezoom.com/algerie-vers-le-livret-foncier-electronique-avec-amlak/>). Its own staff built Amlak in a year. In the last twelve months, the health minister [launched the national rollout of the electronic medical record on 25 July 2026](<https://interlignes.dz/sante-lancement-du-deploiement-du-dossier-medical-electronique-a-travers-les-69-wilayas/>), saying the ministry's own engineers designed and built it. [Dzair Digital Services launched on 5 July 2026](<https://www.algerie360.com/dzair-digital-services-documents-en-ligne/>), and the digitisation commission HCN says [its own services built the checker for documents issued on it](<https://www.elmoudjahid.dz/fr/info-en-continu/portail-national-des-services-numeriques-le-hcn-va-assurer-des-formations-33381>). In March 2025 the Interior Ministry [launched a police-services platform built by the national police's own engineers](<https://www.lactualgerie.com/divers/lancement-dune-plateforme-numerique-pour-les-services-de-police/>).

In the last twelve months, in April 2026, NOSI said [its own specialists were working round the clock on its digital transformation system](<https://www.nosi.gov.eg/ar/News/Pages/2026-04-22.aspx>). They worked with the implementing company, the consultant and the data centre to fix slow performance. The system went live on 24 February 2026. [In June 2021 the World Bank said e-Finance runs the government's financial payments network](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/533491624466169827/pdf/G2P-Payment-Arrangements-in-Egypt-and-COVID-19.pdf>). It is a state-owned enterprise set up in 2005. No source found from 2023 or later says a government body builds or runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

In June 2025 the National Election Board said [its voter and candidate registration applications were operational](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_6739876>). Its own technical team designed them entirely. In the last twelve months, [the state-owned FaydaVerse, not a supplier, has managed the national identity system since 4 August 2026](<https://kanatelevision.com/news/what-is-faydaverse-the-ethiopian-national-id-program-that-became-a-company-and-how-it-plans-to/>). In October 2026 [a cyber drill platform built entirely by INSA's experts was used by 17 institutions](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/8150/ethiopia-s-insa-organises-national-cyber-drill-competition-to-strengthen-institutional-cybersecurity-readiness>). INSA is the state's network security agency. It says [tools it developed are in use across key government agencies](<https://ethiopianbusinessreview.net/innovation-wears-netela-ethiopia-to-build-its-own-versions-of-whatsapp-gmail-and-zoom-citing-tired-of-data-leaks/>).

In January 2026 the delegate budget minister [launched SIGFIP, which he said was developed in-house](<https://gabon-info.com/2026/01/15/le-gabon-reprend-la-main-sur-sa-souverainete-financiere-et-numerique/>). In the last twelve months, in April 2026, the National Assembly [launched GTLAN, a legislative platform ANINF built](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0405-55229-gabon-s-national-assembly-launches-digital-platform-to-modernise-legislative-process>). In August 2026 the budget directorate's own IT unit [launched OLIA, a staff database](<https://www.dgb-gabon.net/actualite-detail/84/details>). On 2 October 2026 the state digital agency ANINF [handed the PROXIGAB platform it built to the SME directorate-general](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-entrepreneuriat-la-plateforme-numerique-proxigab-officiellement-lancee/>). Its own experts designed and developed it.

The Vice President [launched the CitizenApp on 7 October 2024](<https://gna.org.gh/2024/10/bawumia-unveils-new-citizenapp-to-promote-efficiency-in-public-service-delivery/>). The Ghana Revenue Authority and NITA built it with other state agencies, and no contractor is named. In the last twelve months, IMANI wrote in October 2026 that [NITA runs the Government Cloud and the NITA Data Centre](<https://imaniafrica.org/2026/10/the-missing-plumbing-of-the-state-why-ghanas-next-digital-leap-depends-on-a-whole-of-government-data-exchange/>), which ministries and agencies can host on. Not every system is in-house: in April 2025 the communications minister said [the contractor KelniGVG runs the platform monitoring inbound international traffic](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/ghana-news-communication-ministry-saddled-with-debt-strangulating-contracts-minister.html>). No source found since October 2023 names three systems run wholly by government staff. Mature would need three or more systems run, maintained and changed by government staff, with no contractor, by a source from the past three years.

On 20 May 2026 the finance ministry [launched SICOM](<https://www.mef.gov.gn/modernisation-des-finances-publiques-la-guinee-lance-sicom-son-nouvel-outil-numerique-souverain-de-gestion-du-patrimoine-public/>), a public-asset accounting system that connects 24 ministries. The ministry says staff of its IT directorate developed it entirely. No source says who runs it. SICOM is the one launch found in the last twelve months. [In December 2023 a USAID supply chain project trained health ministry staff and two local firms to administer the national eLMIS](<https://www.ghsupplychain.org/news/guinean-computer-scientists-trained-manage-health-logistics-system>). [A decree of 12 April 2022 created ANDE](<https://ande.gov.gn/mission-et-attributions/>), the state digital agency. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

No stage is set. No source found from 2023 or later says government staff run or maintain any of its systems. Five systems have been found, among them [the DHIS2 justice adaptation](<https://www.undp.org/guinea-bissau/blog/e-justice-guinea-bissau-learning-what-works-or-not>) and [SICAJ](<http://web.archive.org/web/20260608181237/https://www.undp.org/guinea-bissau/blog/e-justice-guinea-bissau-going-digital-can-improve-access-justice>). No source found says who runs them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later saying government's own staff run, maintain or built one of its systems.

On 19 November 2025 the Supreme Court [launched its institutional website](<https://ahoraeg.com/sociedad/2025/11/19/la-corte-suprema-de-justicia-presenta-su-pagina-web-institucional/>). The court's own Directorate General of Archives designed it. The GEX case-file platform [was developed by CNIAPGE's own technical team](<https://realequatorialguinea.com/destacado/cniapge-forma-a-funcionarios-de-la-primatura-en-el-uso-de-la-plataforma-de-gestion-de-expedientes/>), and CNIAPGE is rolling it out to the Prime Minister's office. In the last twelve months, in 2026, the Vice-President told the state company GETESA to [plan for its own staff to take over maintenance](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/getesa_presenta_su_plan_de_accion_estrategico_2026-2030>). That work on the telecom network is now contracted out. No source found since October 2023 names three systems run wholly by government staff. Mature would need three or more systems run, maintained and changed by government staff, with no contractor, by a source from the past three years.

In March 2024 Makueni County [launched its Projects Monitoring and Tracking System, built by its in-house ICT team without outside vendors](<https://umanyi.makueni.go.ke/storage/success_stories/68b949613618a_Success_Story.pdf>). ICT Authority Kenya is a state corporation that [runs a network operations centre and a cloud data centre, and designs e-services systems for government](<https://icta.go.ke/faqs>). In October 2024 the Treasury Cabinet Secretary said [the ICT Authority operates eCitizen, collecting for government and paying the service provider](<https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/economy/state-collects-sh127bn-via-e-citizen-4784244>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 names three systems run wholly by government staff. Mature would need three or more systems run, maintained and changed by government staff, with no contractor, by a source from the past three years.

[Liberia Revenue Authority programmers developed the online police clearance platform](<https://gnnliberia.com/lnp-lra-digitize-police-clearance-in-major-reform/>), which was launched at police headquarters on 1 May 2026. It replaced a manual process. That launch is the one found in the last twelve months. In July 2025 the authority said [its own tech team built and launched its online duty-free application platform](<https://revenue.lra.gov.lr/lra-digitizes-rural-customs-offices-rolls-out-online-duty-free-platform/>). The finance ministry's budget system is run differently: in 2024 FrontPageAfrica reported that [the vendor RoviaGate runs and reconfigures it under annual contracts](<https://frontpageafricaonline.com/liberia-frontpageafricas-latest-investigation-unveils-procurement-breach-in-ministry-of-finance-roviagate-contract/>). Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

On 31 July 2025 the Central Bank of Libya said [it developed and runs the Ratibak Lahzi public payroll platform itself](<https://alwasat.ly/news/libya/485074>). In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the Agency for Combating Illegal Migration [unveiled a unified digital system linking its headquarters and branches](<https://libyareview.com/67705/libya-launches-unified-digital-system-to-monitor-migration-operations/>). The agency says its own engineers built it entirely. The technical education ministry's information systems section [is overseeing the update of its electronic archiving system](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=366096&lang=ar>). No source found from 2023 or later says a government agency or state company runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

[Epolice was launched in December 2024](<https://fr.le360.ma/societe/plateforme-epolice-comment-la-dgsn-amorce-sa-transformation-digitale-pour-etre-au-plus-pres-et-en_KBP6WMVA5ZF3ZLZRDOTOE3GSDI/>). Le360 reported in January 2025 that the national police's information systems directorate has digital, development, systems and security teams that run it. The police's own teams built and run it, and no contractor is named. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Epolice serves the police alone. No ministry, agency or state company is found hosting or building systems for other ministries. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

In November 2026 the transport minister said [the ministry's own technicians developed its online platform for reporting irregularities](<https://www.2424.mg/mobilite-urbaine-les-citoyens-invites-a-signaler-les-irregularites-dans-le-secteur-des-transports-via-une-plateforme-numerique>), at no cost to the state budget. Citizens reach it on the ministry's website, and each report gets a code to follow its handling. That platform is the one launch found in the last twelve months. [UNDP's 2025 terms of reference say gendarmerie technicians designed and built the Fichier central](<https://www.ungm.org/Public/Notice/269304>), a register that does not yet hold fingerprint records. No source found since October 2023 names three systems run wholly by government staff. Mature would need three or more systems run, maintained and changed by government staff, with no contractor, by a source from the past three years.

On 17 April 2026 the mines minister presented [a new mining cadastre built entirely by public administration staff](<https://maliactuel.com/secteur-minier-le-president-de-la-transition-preside-la-presentation-du-nouveau-cadastre-minier/>), which held 631 mining titles. In the last twelve months, on 10 February 2026, [online portals for criminal records and nationality certificates were launched](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/public-management/mali-launches-online-criminal-record-and-nationality-certificate-services>). The digital ministry and AGETIC developed them, and no contractor is named. In December 2025 AGETIC, the state ICT agency, [managed 13,441 .ml domain names and 30 registrars](<https://lessor.ml/posts/cyber-espace-le-mali-renforce-sa-viabilite-avec-le-point-ml-69538f175e535>). In February 2025 the justice ministry launched [court case-management software developed at AGETIC](<https://www.maliweb.net/societe/justice/troisieme-edition-de-la-semaine-de-la-justice-le-logiciel-de-gestion-des-dossiers-judiciaires-lance-3093413.html>).

In the last twelve months, INAGE's service catalogue, retrieved on 8 August 2026, [lists server rental, application hosting and application development as services for public bodies](<https://www.inage.gov.mz/?p=2697>). INAGE is the national e-government institute. [INTIC offers the SCDM digital signature service free to government](<https://intic.gov.mz/sistema-de-certificacao-digital-mocambique-registou-crescimento-na-adesao-de-assinaturas-electronicas-em-2024/>), and more than 10 public institutions use it. INTIC says Mozambican professionals implement and manage it. In August 2020 INAGE said it had developed CloudGov, a file storage and sharing system, and it gave no go-live date. No source found says a system built by government staff went live since October 2023. Operating would need a system built by government staff, not a contractor, to go live within the last three years.

[ANRPTS, the population register agency, launched Houwiyeti on 26 December 2023](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/237149>). It takes applications for identity cards, passports and civil-status extracts. The Interior Ministry says [a team of engineers at ANRPTS built the Houwiyeti app](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/292885>), which won the government category of the Africa T-Awards in 2026. In the last twelve months, [the state digital agency AN-État put an AI road-safety system into service on 26 December 2025](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2612-134553-la-mauritanie-met-en-service-une-solution-d-ia-dediee-a-la-securite-routiere>). It covers the whole national road network. No source found since October 2023 names three systems run wholly by government staff. Mature would need three or more systems run, maintained and changed by government staff, with no contractor, by a source from the past three years.

CISD, the Central Information Systems Division of the ministry for information technology, [developed the new Government payroll system entirely in-house, and it took over payroll processing in July 2024](<https://cisd.govmu.org/Documents/Newsletter/Enewsletter%20issue%20No.6.pdf>). All finance sections across government use it. CISD's own unit also [fully rolled out the Bad Weather Allowance System for the fisheries ministry](<https://cisd.govmu.org/Documents/Newsletter/Enewsletter%20issue%20No.6.pdf>) and released the Flight Clearance system, whose three phases have gone live. No contractor is named for any of the three. In 2024 CISD counted 32 application systems under maintenance and four gone live. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

The Malawi Revenue Authority said in October 2026 that [it is developing ITAS II, its second Integrated Tax Administration System, in-house](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/business/mra-credits-ataf-support-for-tax-administration-reforms-data-improvements/article_46cb9644-8810-4649-be0a-d358dbf91606.html>). ITAS II was still being developed at that date, and no launch has been found. That is the one build under way found in the last twelve months. [In April 2025 the Electoral Commission had its ICT Directorate upload 2,563 outstanding voter records onto the Election Management System database](<https://mec.org.mw/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/20250408-Speech-for-press-briefing-on-Voter-Transfers-and-Inspection-of-Voters-Register.pdf>). No source found since October 2023 says a government body builds or runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government agency or state company that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

In June 2024 the Electoral Commission said [its voter registration system is managed under its own IT policies](<https://web.archive.org/web/20240615064053/https://omutumwa.com/2024/06/ecn-explains-slow-start-of-mobile-voter-registration-system/>). A fully-fledged IT Division is entrusted with its systems. On 17 November 2025 the Namibia Revenue Agency [launched Onyofi, a customer service system its own developer built](<https://namibiabusinessreview.com/revenue-agency-launches-customer-service-system/>). The Ministry of Finance [sought consultants to support, maintain and develop the Integrated Financial Management System](<https://cpbn.com.na/index/bid/78>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a government body builds or runs systems for the rest of government. Establishing would need a government body that builds, hosts or runs systems for the rest of government, by a source from 2023 or later.
